name: Eye level
definition: Lens at the subject's eye height, level. Full perceptual data in cam.eye_level.
how: rig.js: cam py at the face; horizon line through the eyes. AI: 'eye-level camera'.
purpose: neutral, equal relationship with the viewer
narrative_function: default 'objective' storytelling; makes deviations (high/low) meaningful by contrast
avoid_when: a power shift should be felt
ai_image_prompt: eye-level camera, horizon through the subject's eyes
ai_video_prompt: Eye-level medium shot, camera locked off at the subject's eye height.
ai_video_notes: Listed in Veo guide (Google-VeoPromptGuide) and Luma key eye_level (Luma-Concepts).
common_mistakes: 'eye level' of the camera operator, not of the subject (child/seated subjects)
check: Horizon/vanishing point passes through the subject's eyes.

name: High angle
definition: Camera above eye level looking down. Evidence (power/weakness, trust) is summarised in cam.high_angle and cam.low_angle: effects are context-dependent and smaller than craft lore claims.
how: rig.js: character lower in frame with a lot of floor; cam py above the face. AI: 'high-angle shot looking down'.
purpose: vulnerability, being watched, overview of action
narrative_function: marks a character as small relative to the situation; 'authorial' surveillance view
emotional_effect: weakness / vulnerability - in narrative context only (va:SevenantsDYdewalle2006) [EVIDENCE, mixed]
avoid_when: a presenter must look confident (direct address)
ai_image_prompt: high-angle shot looking down at a man sitting alone on the floor of an empty room
ai_video_prompt: High-angle shot looking down at a man sitting alone; camera slowly cranes up, making him smaller.
ai_video_notes: Accepted term in Veo guide and Luma key high_angle.
common_mistakes: slight high angle on a talking head reads as 'webcam', not as story
check: Is the angle steep enough to read as intentional (>~20°)? [CRAFT]

name: Low angle
definition: Camera below eye level looking up. See cam.low_angle for the mixed evidence (dominance in story order; lowest trust for direct-address speakers).
how: rig.js: character lower+bigger, floor visible, ceiling cropped, cam py lower than the face. AI: 'low-angle shot'.
purpose: power, threat, heroism, monumentality of a product
narrative_function: marks a rise in power; pairs with a high angle on the opponent
emotional_effect: lower trust for a direct-address speaker (va:BaranowskiHecht2018) [EVIDENCE, medium]
avoid_when: a salesperson talking to camera - trust drops
ai_image_prompt: low-angle shot looking up at a pair of sunglasses on a stone pedestal against a clear blue sky
ai_video_prompt: Low-angle shot looking up at the hero; camera slowly pedestals down, making her loom larger.
ai_video_notes: Veo guide 'low-angle shot'; Luma key low_angle.
check: Is this a power moment, not a trust moment?

name: Bird's-eye / top shot
definition: Directly or nearly directly above. cam.overhead covers flat-lay product use.
how: Needs its own background/art in 2D. AI: 'bird's-eye view, top-down'.
purpose: maps, patterns, fate/God's view, flat lays
narrative_function: removes the horizon - abstracts people into pattern; authorial distance
ai_image_prompt: bird's-eye view, top-down, a person lying on a bed of autumn leaves, arms spread
ai_video_prompt: Top-down bird's-eye view of a person lying in autumn leaves; camera rises straight up slowly.
ai_video_notes: Veo example: 'A bird's-eye view of a vast, intricate maze made of high green hedges.' Luma key overhead.
common_mistakes: AI tilts the 'top-down' into a high oblique; say 'directly overhead, 90 degrees'

name: Worm's-eye / ground level
definition: Camera on or near the ground looking up (worm's-eye) or level along the ground (ground level).
how: AI: 'worm's-eye view from the ground'; rig.js: separate art with strong upward perspective.
purpose: giant scale, childlike/animal viewpoint, dramatic footsteps
ai_image_prompt: worm's-eye view from the pavement, a woman's shoes stepping over the camera, tall buildings converging above
ai_video_prompt: Ground-level shot on the pavement; footsteps approach and step over the camera. Locked-off.
ai_video_notes: Veo lists 'Worm's-eye view'; Luma key ground_level.
common_mistakes: verticals converge strongly - fine if intended, keep the horizon off-frame
check: Does it serve scale/power, or is it a gimmick?

name: Dutch / canted
definition: Camera rolled around the lens axis so the horizon tilts.
how: rig.js: cam.move(t,dur,{rot:4-8}) - raise s so rotated edges stay covered (see FD24 §coverage). AI: 'Dutch angle, tilted horizon'.
narrative_function: marks a scene or moment as psychologically 'off'
use_when: one or two shots at the peak of wrongness (GUIDE.md)
avoid_when: whole scenes - it stops meaning anything

examples.note: Dolly zoom combined with a Dutch angle in a shootout (per Wikipedia's dolly-zoom list)

ai_image_prompt: Dutch angle, horizon tilted about 15 degrees, a man in a narrow corridor under flickering light
ai_video_prompt: Dutch angle medium shot in a narrow corridor; the camera slowly rolls further off level as he backs away.
ai_video_notes: Veo: 'Dutch angle or canted angle'; Luma keys roll_left/roll_right; Kling roll axis.
common_mistakes: tiny tilts (1-3°) look like a mistake, not a choice

name: POV angle
definition: Camera at a character's eye position and direction. Shot unit in shot.pov.
how: Match the character's height; add human sway.
narrative_function: aligns knowledge and feeling with one character
ai_image_prompt: first-person view at adult eye height, hands visible holding a menu
ai_video_prompt: First-person POV walking into a bright shop, slight natural head bob.
check: Height and direction match the looker.

name: Over-the-shoulder angle
definition: Camera behind one character's shoulder toward the other; mirrored in the reverse.
how: Both OTS set-ups on the same side of the axis of action.
narrative_function: shot/reverse-shot - attention follows conversational turns and gaze (Smith2012-AToCC)

examples.note: Smith analyses an 'erroneous' shot/reverse-shot sequence as a deliberate continuity violation

ai_image_prompt: over-the-shoulder shot from behind the man's right shoulder toward the woman
ai_video_prompt: Over-the-shoulder shot; the woman answers and looks down. Locked-off.
ai_video_notes: Veo 'Over-the-shoulder shot'; Luma key over_the_shoulder. AI rarely matches the reverse - generate both from one master still.
common_mistakes: reverse taken from the other side of the line
check: Left/right positions consistent across the pair.

name: Profile
definition: Subject seen at 90° from the side.
how: rig.js side puppets (view:'side'); AI: 'side profile view'.
narrative_function: the viewer is a witness, not addressed
ai_image_prompt: side profile view of a man wearing round tortoiseshell glasses, clean grey background, rim light
ai_video_prompt: Side profile medium close-up; he turns his head slowly toward camera. Locked-off.
ai_video_notes: Turning from profile to front is a common AI morph point - check the glasses' shape mid-turn.

name: Three-quarter
how: Default for faces and products; shows front and side planes.
ai_image_prompt: three-quarter view of a pair of acetate glasses on a mirror surface, soft box light
ai_video_prompt: Three-quarter medium close-up; the woman listens and nods. Slow push-in.
check: Both front and side planes visible.

name: Frontal / direct address
definition: Subject faces the lens; eyes to camera = direct address.
how: Lens on the subject's axis; eye level for trust (va:BaranowskiHecht2018).
purpose: presenter, testimonial, symmetry, confrontation with the viewer
narrative_function: breaks or reinforces the fourth wall
emotional_effect: directness; trust highest at eye level for direct address (va:BaranowskiHecht2018) [EVIDENCE, medium]
avoid_when: fiction characters looking into the lens by accident
ai_image_prompt: frontal symmetrical shot, a woman looking directly into the lens, centered, eye-level
ai_video_prompt: Frontal medium shot, she looks straight into the lens and speaks. Locked-off at eye level.

name: Rear / from behind
how: Follow shots, back-of-head into a reveal.
purpose: mystery, following, sharing what the character sees next
narrative_function: withholds the face; invites the viewer to step into the character
ai_image_prompt: from behind, a woman with a backpack stands at the edge of a cliff overlooking a valley
ai_video_prompt: From behind, the camera follows a woman through a doorway into a bright room, gimbal shot.
ai_video_notes: Following-from-behind is a semantic primitive ('follow') that geometric trackers miss (Lin2025-CameraBench).
check: Is the face withheld for a reason?

name: Shoulder level
definition: Lens slightly below the eyes (shoulder height), looking almost level.
how: Real: lower the camera ~10-20 cm below the eyes. rig.js: cam py slightly below the face.
purpose: a subtle, almost invisible lift in stature - more flattering than strict eye level for actors [CRAFT]
narrative_function: quietly strengthens a character without reading as a 'low angle'
ai_image_prompt: medium close-up, camera at shoulder height looking very slightly up at the woman
ai_video_prompt: Medium close-up from shoulder height, very slight upward angle; locked-off.
ai_video_notes: Models rarely distinguish this from eye level - treat as untestable in AI; use in 2D/real footage.
check: Ceiling barely visible; jaw not exaggerated.

name: Hip level
definition: Lens at hip height, usually level; associated with Westerns' draw/gun level and with Ozu-style low camera [CRAFT, unverified example].
how: Real: camera at ~1 m; rig.js: py near the waist line with the floor visible.
narrative_function: brings hands and objects into the drama
use_when: hands handing over objects, counters, desks
ai_image_prompt: camera at hip height, level, a shop counter in the foreground with hands passing a pair of glasses
ai_video_prompt: Hip-level shot along the counter; hands pass a glasses case across. Locked-off.
common_mistakes: tilting up toward the face - becomes a low angle
check: Lens level; horizon at hip height.

name: Knee level
definition: Lens at knee height, level or slightly up.
how: Real: low mount / hi-hat. rig.js: floor dominant, py near the knees.
purpose: child or pet viewpoint, feet and walking, comic smallness
narrative_function: viewpoint of a small being; underlines size difference
ai_image_prompt: camera at knee height, a small dog's viewpoint looking up at a person's legs at a shop door
ai_video_prompt: Knee-height tracking shot following a small dog into a shop, gimbal, smooth.
check: Height is motivated by a character or a gag.

name: Aerial oblique (drone)
definition: High camera (drone/heli) looking down at 20-60° with the horizon visible - unlike bird's-eye.
how: AI: 'aerial drone shot'; Luma keys aerial / aerial_drone. 2D: separate painted plate with parallax layers.
purpose: geography of a city/landscape, opening scale
ai_image_prompt: aerial drone shot at 45 degrees over Hua Hin beach at golden hour, horizon visible at the top
ai_video_prompt: Sweeping aerial drone shot flying forward over a beach town at golden hour, smooth and steady.
ai_video_notes: Veo example: 'Sweeping aerial drone shot flying over a tropical island chain'. Wide aerial views hide AI artefacts well.
common_mistakes: fake text on signs in AI cities

name: Selfie / arm's-length
definition: Phone-camera position at arm's length, usually slightly above, subject looking into the lens.
how: Wide lens (~24-26 mm eq.) at ~50-60 cm. Luma key 'selfie'.
purpose: UGC/creator look, vlogs, authenticity in social ads
emotional_effect: close camera distance makes faces rated less trustworthy/attractive (va:BryanPeronaAdolphs2012) [EVIDENCE]
use_when: creator-style ads, testimonials meant to look unpolished
avoid_when: beauty/portrait shots where face shape matters - distance distorts
ai_image_prompt: selfie photo at arm's length, slightly above eye level, a young man wearing new glasses smiling in a shop mirror light
ai_video_prompt: Selfie-style handheld video at arm's length; he talks to camera while walking out of the shop.
common_mistakes: using it for premium product beauty
